newsitem.title: BOSNIA: New attack on peace forces in Croat Mostar - NATO.
newsitem.headline: New attack on peace forces in Croat Mostar - NATO.

text.p: NATO said on Saturday that a grenade was thrown at an Italian peacekeeping vehicle patrolling the Croat-controlled western sector of Mostar in Bosnia overnight, the second attack in as many days.
Four Italian soldiers were unhurt and their vehicle was undamaged. The attackers escaped by car. A NATO spokesman said the identity of the assailants was unknown.
Two nights before, five Spanish soldiers escaped injury when their vehicle was hit by a 64 mm anti-tank rocket in the Croat sector of the ethnically polarised Bosnian city.
Mostar, south of Sarajevo, is divided between Moslems and Croats, a legacy of an 11-month war fought in 1993 that ended with a U.S.-brokered agreement to form a federation in 1994.

Chronic tensions between the communities were aggravated by a February 10 incident when a Croat mob, some of them policemen, attacked a group of Moslems who tried to visit a cemetery in west Mostar. One Moslem was killed and 22 were injured.
NATO, international police monitors and Western diplomats generally blamed Croat ultra-nationalists for the clash and six Croat policemen have since been suspended from duty and charged with assault.

But Croatian state media said on Saturday that Mostar Croat authorities had also filed charges against 11 Moslems, including east Mostar mayor Safet Orucevic, "on a founded suspicion of having committed criminal acts" in the clash.
They said the charges accused the 11 Moslems of having "organised and participated" in the clash.
